text: In categorical logic, a model of a Lawvere theory $\mathbb{T}$ in a category $\mathcal{C}$ is defined to be:
choices: A left adjoint to an inclusion $\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{T}$
explanation: The chapter defines a model of $\mathbb{T}$ in $\mathcal{C}$ as a product-preserving functor $\mathbb{T}\to\mathcal{C}$; preserving finite products is exactly what lets the abstract operations act on genuine tuples. An arbitrary functor need not respect the operations, colimit-preservation is the wrong (dual) condition, and no adjoint to an inclusion is part of the definition.
